works.title: Antagonist
works.description:
"Before the duo can react, the crescent of adversaries splits down the middle, revealing an awful, HORRIBLE THING. Facing them, a skinless amalgam of flesh and elegant robotic material in the shape of a person, stands in the middle of the room. A haunted, cursed skull bears cold, metal teeth; its eye sockets possess a beady, piercing red light that rots through the duo's souls."

Concept art of the 'main big bad boss' of my Trepidation project. A tiny machine 'mysteriously' propagated into a normal person's brain, which started taking over their body. Bone was converted to metal, and muscle converted to gel-like synthetics.

1st image is the cinematic perspective, the 2nd image is the POV. Image 3 is a viewport look, and image 4 and 5 are concept art from long, long ago.

A stab at a corporate-minimalist style.

The QR-code-style glyphs come from the language I've designed for my Trepidation project. These simple posters are designs I can easily paste into established scenes to give the feel I'm looking for.

works.title: 4-Arms vs the Scientist
works.description:
"The Four-Armed Prisoner rushes and PINS the Scientist to the WALL. HIS TOP SET PRESSES HIS FOREARMS ABOVE HIM, While the bottom set JACKHAMMERS PUNCHES into his TORSO. With each meaty THWACK, the Scientist's back EXPLODES BLOOD ONTO THE WALL."

An illustration of a scene from my Trepidation project. I don't look highly on this piece; I think it's overall a little too indiscernible. I really wanted to showcase all four arms while also detailing a sense of claustrophobia from the Scientist's (left) perspective.

I made a crude 3d scene to try out various angles and this is what I landed on.

Canonically takes place at the same moment in the same room as "Colleague_Face". I was inspired to make this based off the turnout of "Scientist_Winged".

works.title: Colleague Face
works.description:
A render of a scene from my Trepidation project. Sculpted manually with 99% procedural materials (the LED panel wall in the back uses an image texture. That's it).

This piece involved use of almost every tab within the blender suite, which seriously tested my familarities and capability within the software. Although procedural, I still had to work with UVs on the character's skin and undershirt. The seam edges of the undershirt were done with geometry nodes, as well. 

2nd image excludes the graphics.

3rd image was the initial render, for the sake of framing.

4th video was a lackluster animation I whipped up a while later. Because the character was sculpted, I couldn't animate them at all; I had no further expectations and moved on to new projects.

works.title: Procedural Land
works.description:
A messy attempt at a vast expanse. The ground is a single material with a thouroughly subdivided plane. The clouds are also procedural.

The 2nd image was my first render. Had to play around with a lot of the values to get something I was happy with, It also lacks any post-processing.

I forsee a remake of this shader material, something far more elaborate which could account for multiple biome types.

This render was made 2026-06, but this section showcases the cards themselves more than the render.

I imagined the skull's eyes as portals the gun was half inside. It might be interpreted differently. I think it looks cool either way.

works.title: Winged Scientist
works.description:
A non-canon depiction of a character from my Trepidation project.

This artwork originally existed only as linework and messy colors from two years prior (2nd image). I felt like drawing but didn't want to think of a pose so I dug this up, dusted it off, and cleaned it up.

Images 3 & 4 - The cityscape in the background was made in blender with a shader to simulate black outlines. After rendering, I did a lot of work to fix the colors and materials to have it fit in with the rest of the scene. The rings around the planet were also rendered in 3D, but as a separate layer from the cityscape. Everything else was done in 2D.

The entire artwork, from start to finish, was inspired by 'Reaper Hank' by Rhunyc on Newgrounds (5th image).

works.title: Skull 02
works.description: A stylized design possibly fit for an album cover.

works.title: Fossil Walker
works.description:
Character art for a card in my TCG Concept, Exul Omnium. A collection of desert bones, traversing a sandstorm.

This card's abilities allow give the player a 40% chance to destroy a random card from the player's hand whenever it deals damage. It also takes more-than-usual damage from enemies.

This card features an experimental 'Glass' design which shows off more of the card art.

works.title: Frozen Aperture
works.description: Depicting a concept I had for a while; what Aperture Science from Value's Portal franchise would look like during the wintertime. Frigid, icy, industrial spaces deep underground.

works.title: Zero-Point Blade
works.description:
A sword that can cut through any material. The idea here is the orange strip "deletes" anything that touches it, and the blue energy harnesses and stretches the strip into a blade shape. The circuitry in the hilt and blade controls this action, and the pommel is a battery. 

I also made an animation depicting the effect with some SFX.

works.title: Scientist Spine
works.description:
A stylized depiction of the Scientist's cybernetic augment in my trepidation project. When making the materials in blender, I also experimented with an X-ray style design (image 2).

Image 3 is a viewport screenshot, and Image 4 was my first take on the graphic design, which I later reworked into Image 1.

works.title: Pyroclastic Elemental
works.description:
Character art for a card in my TCG Concept, Exul Omnium. A living plume of fire. It has two eyes looking forward, which maybe didn't turn out too well.

This card's abilities dictate the card can only stay alive for two turns, but every fire type it defeats extends that timer by one turn. It has a 50% to deal bonus damage to surrounding enemies, and it also explodes on death.

It's working name was "Fire Elemental".

works.title: Scientist Thermal
works.description: A heavily stylized depction of the Scientist character from my Trepidation project. Heavily inspired from the use of color from the works of Spazgunk on Newgrounds (images 2 and 3)

works.title: Spiderman 2099
works.description:
Made a week before the release of Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse, because I liked the concept of the character. I knew nothing about him expect that he was probably the villian. After coming out of the theatre seeing him in action, I noticed about a dozen inaccuracies with my depiction of him. But, I never brought myself to alter the final piece.

The hexagons in the background were made in blender (image 2), the lots of filters and effects and edits were made to match it with the subject. I think it help sell the movie's aesthetic of 2D and 3D styles clashing.

works.title: Creeping Shade
works.description:
Character art for a card in my TCG Concept, Exul Omnium. Sticky sickly smoke suspending a skeleton inside it.

This card's abilities give it an 80% chance to deal overkill damage to nearby enemies.

It's working name was "Shade Watcher".

works.title: Dimension Jumper
works.description:
Character art for a card in my TCG Concept, Exul Omnium. Some kind of alien that can easily slip between dimensional spaces. It has four eyes, which may not be too clear.

This card's abilities allow it to freely travel between your controlled lands, and upon death it has a 1/3 chance to respawn in any of those lands.

works.title: Pixel Combat Sprites
works.description:
An extensive stylization of mine. Insipred from the works of Mostaza (7th image). 

This collection of sci-fi guns was a direct response to the initial collection I made two years prior (2nd image). I was not satisfied with a handful of designs from the original collection, but I would rather make new designs over remaking the old ones.

I've made a LOT of sprites with this stylization.

works.title: Nephilim
works.description:
"The HEXTILLE PATTERN across the Nephilim's skin begins to glow RED HOT, and he starts WRITHING IN PAIN! He's excreting LITERS of blood -- his SMOLDERING flesh is luckily CAUTERIZING the majority of these lacerations. The thrashing slows... The wiring loses its HEAT... Still standing, the RAVAGED Nephilim angrily looks around the room for answers. A Dev timidly approaches, and offers some kind of illustration on a clipboard in one hand and a communication device in the other. The Nephilim looks down at him. He makes a MIDDLE FINGER AND PUNCHES the Dev, CRUMPLING him into a pile of flesh against the floor!"

Concept art for a 10-foot tall character in my Trepidation project. The hextille of wiring would've given his skin LiDAR-like depth stimuli, allowing him to sense impacts and react before they touch him. This would obviously not be very necessary to a beast of this caliber -- the hextille wiring was actually supposed to go in human-sized units, but the devs couldn't develop the technology to fit properly, it needed to be too dense. So a larger unit was created purely to see the current technology work under ideal bodily proportions. However, the prototype didn't work exactly as planned...

Slide 3: A propaganda-style graphic depitcing the hextille-LiDAR technology as sleek and idealistic.

Timeline: Slide 1 - Feb 23, Slide 2 - Feb 26, Slide 3 - Feb 24
